Question: Which clause filters groups after GROUP BY?
Options:
A. WHERE
B. HAVING
C. ORDER BY
D. LIMIT
Marked answer: B. HAVING
Why: HAVING filters groups after the rows are grouped and counted. WHERE filters single rows before grouping.

Question: A LEFT JOIN from customers to orders returns…
Options:
A. Every customer, with empty order columns where there is no order
B. Only customers who have orders
C. Only orders that have a customer
D. Every pairing of every customer with every order
Marked answer: A. Every customer, with empty order columns where there is no order
Why: A LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the left table and fills the right table's columns with NULL where nothing matches.

Question: What does COUNT(column) leave out?
Options:
A. Repeated values
B. Zeros
C. Nothing: it counts every row
D. NULL values
Marked answer: D. NULL values
Why: COUNT(column) counts the rows where that column is not NULL. COUNT(*) counts every row.

Question: Which keyword removes repeated rows from a query's result?
Options:
A. UNIQUE
B. GROUP
C. DISTINCT
D. DIFFERENT
Marked answer: C. DISTINCT
Why: SELECT DISTINCT returns each different row once. UNIQUE is a constraint on a table, not part of a SELECT.

Question: What does len({1, 2, 2, 3}) return?
Options:
A. 4
B. 3
C. 2
D. An error
Why: Curly braces with values make a set, and a set keeps one copy of each value: 1, 2 and 3.

Question: Which of these can be a dictionary key?
Options:
A. A tuple of numbers, such as (1, 2)
B. A list, such as [1, 2]
C. Another dictionary
D. A set
Marked answer: A. A tuple of numbers, such as (1, 2)
Why: Keys must be hashable, which means they cannot change. Tuples of numbers can't change; lists, dictionaries and sets can.

Question: What does "data"[1:3] return?
Options:
A. "da"
B. "ata"
C. "dat"
D. "at"
Marked answer: D. "at"
Why: Slicing starts at index 1 and stops before index 3, so it takes the characters at 1 and 2: "a" and "t".

Question: Which line opens a file so it is closed even if an error happens?
Options:
A. f = open("data.csv")
B. f.read("data.csv")
C. with open("data.csv") as f:
D. import data.csv
Marked answer: C. with open("data.csv") as f:
Why: A with block closes the file when the block ends, whether it ends normally or with an error.

Question: Which command shows the line-by-line changes you have not staged yet?
Options:
A. git log
B. git diff
C. git show
D. git branch
Marked answer: B. git diff
Why: git diff with no arguments compares your working files with what is staged. git log lists commits.

Question: What does git pull do?
Options:
A. Fetches the remote branch and merges it (or rebases) into yours
B. Uploads your commits to the remote
C. Throws away your local changes
D. Makes a new branch
Marked answer: A. Fetches the remote branch and merges it (or rebases) into yours
Why: git pull is git fetch followed by a merge, or a rebase if you set it so. git push uploads.

Question: You need to undo a commit that is already on a shared branch. The safe choice is…
Options:
A. git reset --hard, then force-push
B. Delete the branch and start again
C. git commit --amend
D. git revert with that commit
Marked answer: D. git revert with that commit
Why: git revert adds a new commit that undoes the old one, so nobody else's history is rewritten.

Question: Which file lists the paths Git should not track?
Options:
A. .gitconfig
B. .gitkeep
C. .gitignore
D. README.md
Marked answer: C. .gitignore
Why: .gitignore lists files and folders Git leaves out, such as build output and local secrets.

Question: Which command shows running processes and their CPU use, updating live?
Options:
A. ls
B. top
C. cat
D. chmod
Marked answer: B. top
Why: top shows processes sorted by CPU use and refreshes every few seconds. htop is a friendlier version where installed.

Question: What does chmod 644 report.txt allow?
Options:
A. The owner reads and writes; everyone else only reads
B. Everyone reads, writes and runs it
C. Only the owner can run it
D. Nobody can read it
Marked answer: A. The owner reads and writes; everyone else only reads
Why: Each digit is owner, group, others. 6 is read and write, 4 is read only.

Question: Which command finds the lines containing "error" in app.log?
Options:
A. find error app.log
B. cd error app.log
C. mv error app.log
D. grep error app.log
Marked answer: D. grep error app.log
Why: grep prints the lines of a file that match a pattern. find looks for files by name or type.

Question: What does cd .. do?
Options:
A. Goes to your home folder
B. Lists hidden files
C. Moves up one folder
D. Deletes the current folder
Marked answer: C. Moves up one folder
Why: Two dots mean the parent folder. cd on its own, or cd ~, goes home.

Question: What is the difference between an image and a container?
Options:
A. They are two names for the same thing
B. An image is a read-only template; a container is a running copy of it
C. A container is a template; an image is what runs
D. Images run only on Linux; containers run anywhere
Marked answer: B. An image is a read-only template; a container is a running copy of it
Why: You build an image once and can start many containers from it, each with its own writable layer.

Question: Which file describes how to build an image?
Options:
A. Dockerfile
B. docker-compose.yml
C. package.json
D. .dockerignore
Marked answer: A. Dockerfile
Why: A Dockerfile lists the steps to build an image. A compose file describes how to run several containers together.

Question: What does docker run -p 8080:80 nginx do?
Options:
A. Port 80 on your machine reaches port 8080 in the container
B. It starts two containers, one on each port
C. It runs nginx on port 8080 inside the container
D. Port 8080 on your machine reaches port 80 in the container
Marked answer: D. Port 8080 on your machine reaches port 80 in the container
Why: The -p option is host port first, then container port.

Question: Files a container writes outside any volume…
Options:
A. Are kept forever on the host
B. Are saved into the image
C. Are lost when the container is removed
D. Are shared with every other container
Marked answer: C. Are lost when the container is removed
Why: A container's own layer goes with the container. Data that must stay goes in a volume or a bind mount.

Question: Which HTTP method should only read and never change anything on the server?
Options:
A. POST
B. GET
C. DELETE
D. PATCH
Marked answer: B. GET
Why: GET is a safe method: it asks for data. POST, PATCH and DELETE change things.

Question: Which status code usually answers a POST that created something?
Options:
A. 201 Created
B. 200 OK
C. 204 No Content
D. 404 Not Found
Marked answer: A. 201 Created
Why: 201 says something new was created, often with a Location header pointing at it.

Question: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
Options:
A. 401: you aren't allowed; 403: we don't know who you are
B. Both mean the server is down
C. Both mean the page doesn't exist
D. 401: we don't know who you are; 403: we know, and you aren't allowed
Marked answer: D. 401: we don't know who you are; 403: we know, and you aren't allowed
Why: 401 Unauthorized asks for valid credentials. 403 Forbidden means the credentials are fine but the action isn't allowed.

Question: Which method should have the same effect whether it is sent once or twice?
Options:
A. POST
B. Neither of them
C. PUT
D. Only methods without a body
Marked answer: C. PUT
Why: PUT replaces a resource with what you send, so repeating it changes nothing more. Two POSTs can create two records.

Question: What does continuous integration mean?
Options:
A. Releasing once a quarter after a long test phase
B. Merging small changes often, with an automatic build and tests on each one
C. Writing the tests after the release
D. Everyone working on one shared server
Marked answer: B. Merging small changes often, with an automatic build and tests on each one
Why: CI finds problems early because every change is built and tested as soon as it is pushed.

Question: Tests fail in the pipeline on a pull request. What usually happens?
Options:
A. The merge is blocked until the tests pass
B. It merges anyway and is fixed later
C. Production is rolled back
D. The repository is locked for everyone
Marked answer: A. The merge is blocked until the tests pass
Why: Branch protection makes a passing pipeline a condition for merging, so broken code stays out of the main branch.

Question: Where should a password or deploy key used by a pipeline be kept?
Options:
A. In the repository, next to the code
B. In the README
C. In a commit message
D. In the CI system's secret store
Marked answer: D. In the CI system's secret store
Why: Secret stores keep the value out of the code and the logs and let you change it without a commit.

Question: Continuous delivery and continuous deployment differ how?
Options:
A. Deployment has the manual step; delivery is automatic
B. They mean exactly the same
C. Delivery keeps every change ready to release with a manual step; deployment releases every passing change automatically
D. Delivery skips the tests
Marked answer: C. Delivery keeps every change ready to release with a manual step; deployment releases every passing change automatically
Why: Both build and test every change. Continuous deployment also releases it without a person pressing a button.

Question: Five salaries in lakh: 3, 4, 4, 5 and 50. Which number describes a typical salary best?
Options:
A. The mean
B. The median
C. The range
D. The maximum
Marked answer: B. The median
Why: The median, 4, isn't pulled up by the one very high salary. The mean, 13.2, is.

Question: What is the median of 2, 7, 4, 9 and 5?
Why: Sorted, the values are 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, and the middle one is 5. 5.4 is the mean.

Question: A test gives a p-value of 0.03. What does that mean?
Options:
A. There is a 3% chance there is no effect
B. The effect is 3% in size
C. We are 97% sure the result matters
D. If there were no real effect, results at least this extreme would come up about 3% of the time
Marked answer: D. If there were no real effect, results at least this extreme would come up about 3% of the time
Why: A p-value is about the data assuming no effect. It is not the chance the effect is real, and it says nothing about size.

Question: Two measures have a correlation of 0.9. What does that show?
Options:
A. One causes the other
B. They are unrelated
C. They move together strongly
D. One is 90% of the other
Marked answer: C. They move together strongly
Why: A correlation close to 1 means a strong straight-line link. It says nothing on its own about cause.

Question: Which function finds a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from another column of that row?
Options:
A. SUMIF
B. VLOOKUP
C. CONCAT
D. LEN
Marked answer: B. VLOOKUP
Why: VLOOKUP looks down the first column. XLOOKUP and INDEX with MATCH do the same job more flexibly.

Question: The formula =A1*$B$1 is copied down a column. Which part stays the same?
Options:
A. $B$1
B. A1
C. Both of them
D. Neither of them
Why: Dollar signs fix the column and the row, so $B$1 stays put while A1 becomes A2, A3 and so on.

Question: Which tool summarises sales by region and month without writing formulas?
Options:
A. Freeze Panes
B. Text to Columns
C. Format Painter
D. A PivotTable
Marked answer: D. A PivotTable
Why: A PivotTable groups and totals rows by the fields you drag in, and updates when you refresh it.

Question: What does =COUNTIF(A:A, ">100") return?
Options:
A. The total of the values above 100
B. The first value above 100
C. How many cells in column A are above 100
D. TRUE if any value is above 100
Marked answer: C. How many cells in column A are above 100
Why: COUNTIF counts the cells that meet the condition. SUMIF would add them up.

Question: A city column holds "Mumbai", "mumbai " and "MUMBAI". What do you do first?
Options:
A. Delete those rows
B. Trim the spaces and make the case the same
C. Replace them with the most common city
D. Leave them; they mean the same
Marked answer: B. Trim the spaces and make the case the same
Why: Left as they are, they count as three cities in any group or chart. Trimming and one case make them one.

Question: 2% of rows have no age. What is a sensible first step?
Options:
A. Find out why they are missing, then choose to drop or fill them
B. Delete the whole age column
C. Fill them with zero
D. Leave them out of the report without saying so
Marked answer: A. Find out why they are missing, then choose to drop or fill them
Why: Whether values are missing at random decides what is safe. Zero would pull every average down.

Question: Two rows are the same in every column, including the order id. They are most likely…
Options:
A. Two real orders
B. Two different customers
C. A formatting problem
D. A duplicate to check and remove
Marked answer: D. A duplicate to check and remove
Why: An id is meant to be unique, so a repeated row with the same id is usually loaded twice. Check the source before deleting.

Question: An order date column mixes 03/04/2026 and 2026-04-03. What is the risk?
Options:
A. There is no risk
B. The dates sort faster
C. 03/04 can be read as 3 April or as 4 March
D. The spreadsheet deletes them
Marked answer: C. 03/04 can be read as 3 April or as 4 March
Why: Day and month order differs by country. Convert every date to one format, such as 2026-04-03, before you work with them.

Question: Which chart shows monthly revenue over two years most clearly?
Options:
A. A pie chart
B. A line chart
C. A scatter plot
D. A donut chart
Marked answer: B. A line chart
Why: A line chart shows change over time. Pie and donut charts show parts of one whole.

Question: Which chart compares sales across 8 product categories best?
Options:
A. A bar chart
B. A pie chart with 8 slices
C. A line chart
D. A 3D pie chart
Marked answer: A. A bar chart
Why: Bars of one length scale are easy to compare. Eight pie slices are hard to tell apart, and 3D makes it worse.

Question: A bar chart's value axis starts at 90 instead of 0. What does that do?
Options:
A. Makes the bars more accurate
B. Changes nothing
C. Makes the chart easier to print
D. Makes the differences look bigger than they are
Marked answer: D. Makes the differences look bigger than they are
Why: Bar length should match the value, so bar charts start at zero. A cut axis exaggerates small gaps.

Question: To see how ad spend relates to sales across 200 shops, use…
Options:
A. A pie chart
B. A stacked bar chart
C. A scatter plot
D. A gauge
Marked answer: C. A scatter plot
Why: A scatter plot puts one dot per shop, so you can see a trend, clusters and odd shops at a glance.

Question: Which AWS service stores files as objects in buckets?
Options:
A. EC2
B. S3
C. RDS
D. Lambda
Marked answer: B. S3
Why: S3 is object storage. EC2 runs servers, RDS runs managed databases and Lambda runs functions.

Question: Which AWS service gives you virtual servers?
Options:
A. EC2
B. S3
C. IAM
D. CloudFront
Marked answer: A. EC2
Why: EC2 instances are virtual machines you choose the size and system of.

Question: What is IAM used for?
Options:
A. Storing backups
B. Sending email
C. Running a website's DNS
D. Deciding who can do what in your AWS account
Marked answer: D. Deciding who can do what in your AWS account
Why: IAM holds users, roles and policies. Route 53 does DNS, SES sends email.

Question: What is the safest way to let an app on EC2 read from S3?
Options:
A. Put access keys in the app's code
B. Make the bucket public
C. Attach an IAM role to the instance
D. Share the account's root password
Marked answer: C. Attach an IAM role to the instance
Why: A role gives the instance short-lived credentials that change on their own, with no keys to leak.

Question: Which data structure gives O(1) average time for checking whether an item exists?
Options:
A. Sorted array
B. Hash set
C. Linked list
D. Binary heap
Marked answer: B. Hash set
Why: A hash set looks items up by their hash in constant time on average. A sorted array needs O(log n) binary search, and a linked list or heap needs a scan.

Question: Which principle hides an object's internal data behind methods?
Options:
A. Inheritance
B. Polymorphism
C. Abstraction
D. Encapsulation
Marked answer: D. Encapsulation
Why: Encapsulation keeps fields private and exposes behaviour through methods, so internal data can change without breaking callers.

Question: A unit test calls a real payment gateway over the network. What is the main problem?
Options:
A. It is slow and can fail for reasons outside the code
B. It improves coverage too much
C. It makes the test too short
D. It cannot use assertions
Marked answer: A. It is slow and can fail for reasons outside the code
Why: Network calls make tests slow and flaky. Unit tests should replace external services with stubs or mocks.

Question: Which collection keeps keys in sorted order?
Options:
A. HashMap
B. TreeMap
C. LinkedList
D. ArrayList
Marked answer: B. TreeMap
Why: TreeMap stores keys in a red-black tree, so they stay sorted. HashMap keeps no order, and the lists are not key-value maps.

Question: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?
Options:
A. "null"
B. "undefined"
C. "object"
D. "number"
Marked answer: C. "object"
Why: typeof null returns "object" because of a long-standing quirk in the language. Check for null with === null instead.

Question: Which smart pointer allows only one owner of an object?
Options:
A. shared_ptr
B. weak_ptr
C. auto_ptr
D. unique_ptr
Marked answer: D. unique_ptr
Why: unique_ptr has sole ownership and can only be moved, not copied. shared_ptr allows many owners, and auto_ptr is removed from modern C++.

Question: An employee earns ₹9 lakh a year and the band midpoint is ₹10 lakh. What is the compa-ratio?
Why: Compa-ratio is salary divided by the midpoint: 9 ÷ 10 = 0.90, so the person sits 10% below the middle of the band.

Question: In a salary survey, what does the 50th percentile show?
Options:
A. The highest salary reported
B. The average of the top half
C. The figure half the reported salaries fall below
D. The lowest salary reported
Marked answer: C. The figure half the reported salaries fall below
Why: The 50th percentile is the median: half the data points sit below it and half above, so a few very high salaries don't pull it up the way they pull up the mean.

Question: What does a merit matrix usually set?
Options:
A. The increment % by performance rating and position in the band
B. The number of leaves by grade
C. The notice period by level
D. The bonus paid to the sales team only
Marked answer: A. The increment % by performance rating and position in the band
Why: A merit matrix gives a higher increment to better ratings and to people lower in their band, so pay moves towards the midpoint for good performers.

Question: Survey data was collected on 1 April. Increments take effect on 1 October and the market moves about 8% a year. What should you do with the data?
Options:
A. Use it as it is
B. Cut it by 8%
C. Ignore the survey
D. Age it forward by about 4% to October
Marked answer: D. Age it forward by about 4% to October
Why: Ageing moves survey figures to the date you use them: half a year at 8% a year is about 4%, so the comparison isn't out of date.

Question: A band has a minimum of ₹8 lakh and a maximum of ₹12 lakh. What is the midpoint?
Options:
A. ₹9 lakh
B. ₹11 lakh
C. ₹10 lakh
D. ₹12 lakh
Marked answer: C. ₹10 lakh
Why: The midpoint is halfway between the minimum and the maximum: (8 + 12) ÷ 2 = ₹10 lakh.

Question: A band runs from ₹8 lakh to ₹12 lakh. What is its range spread?
Why: Range spread is (maximum − minimum) ÷ minimum: (12 − 8) ÷ 8 = 0.5, or 50%.

Question: What is a 'red-circled' employee?
Options:
A. Someone on a performance improvement plan
B. Someone paid below the band minimum
C. Someone serving notice
D. Someone paid above the band maximum
Marked answer: D. Someone paid above the band maximum
Why: Red-circled means paid above the band's maximum; green-circled means paid below its minimum.

Question: Why do the salary bands of neighbouring grades usually overlap?
Options:
A. To make every grade pay the same
B. So a strong performer in a lower grade can earn more than a new joiner in the grade above
C. Because the law requires it
D. So that no one ever needs a promotion
Marked answer: B. So a strong performer in a lower grade can earn more than a new joiner in the grade above
Why: Overlap lets pay reward experience within a grade, while the higher midpoint of the next grade still rewards promotion.

Skill: Employee benefits and group insurance programmes
Question: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, after how many years of continuous service does an employee usually become eligible for gratuity?
Options:
A. One
B. Three
C. Five
D. Ten
Marked answer: C. Five
Why: The Act sets five years of continuous service as the usual condition, with exceptions such as death or disablement.

Skill: Employee benefits and group insurance programmes
Question: What does a TPA do in a group health insurance policy?
Options:
A. Sets salary bands
B. Handles claims and cashless approvals for the insurer
C. Pays provident fund to employees
D. Audits the company's accounts
Marked answer: B. Handles claims and cashless approvals for the insurer
Why: A third-party administrator processes claims, issues health cards and approves cashless treatment on the insurer's behalf.

Skill: Employee benefits and group insurance programmes
Question: What is the claims ratio of a group health policy?
Options:
A. Claims paid divided by premium earned
B. Number of employees divided by claims
C. Premium divided by number of employees
D. Claims rejected divided by claims made
Marked answer: A. Claims paid divided by premium earned
Why: It is claims paid over premium earned. A ratio well above 100% means the insurer paid out more than it took in, so expect a higher renewal quote.

Skill: Employee benefits and group insurance programmes
Question: Which of these is a statutory benefit in India rather than a company choice?
Options:
A. Gym membership
B. Group health top-up cover
C. Meal vouchers
D. Employees' Provident Fund for covered establishments
Marked answer: D. Employees' Provident Fund for covered establishments
Why: EPF is required under the EPF and Miscellaneous Provisions Act for covered establishments; the others are benefits a company may choose to give.

Question: What is a content calendar mainly used for?
Options:
A. Tracking employee leave
B. Planning what to publish, where and when, with owners
C. Billing clients for articles
D. Storing passwords for social accounts
Marked answer: B. Planning what to publish, where and when, with owners
Why: A content calendar plans topics, channels, dates and owners, so publishing is steady and nothing clashes or slips.

Question: Which goal fits a 'top of the funnel' blog post best?
Options:
A. Closing a sale with a discount code
B. Renewing existing customers
C. Making new readers aware of a problem and the brand
D. Collecting payment details
Marked answer: C. Making new readers aware of a problem and the brand
Why: Top-of-funnel content attracts people who don't know the brand yet; offers and renewals belong further down the funnel.

Question: A newsletter has a 30% open rate and a 1% click rate. Where should you look first to get more clicks?
Options:
A. The subject line only
B. The sender's name
C. The send time only
D. The content and call to action inside the email
Marked answer: D. The content and call to action inside the email
Why: People are opening it, so the subject line works. Few clicks points to the body: relevance, layout and a clear call to action.

Question: What is evergreen content?
Options:
A. Content that stays useful for a long time
B. News about a festival sale
C. A post that expires after 24 hours
D. Content written only for paid ads
Marked answer: A. Content that stays useful for a long time
Why: Evergreen pieces, such as how-to guides, keep bringing readers long after they are published, unlike timely news.

Skill: SEO content writing and keyword research
Question: What does search intent mean?
Options:
A. The number of searches a keyword gets
B. What the person searching actually wants to find or do
C. The cost of a keyword in ads
D. How fast a page loads
Marked answer: B. What the person searching actually wants to find or do
Why: Intent is the need behind the search: to learn, compare, buy or reach a site. A page ranks best when it matches that need.

Skill: SEO content writing and keyword research
Question: Which HTML element is usually the clickable headline in search results?
Options:
A. The meta keywords tag
B. The H3 heading
C. The image alt text
D. The title tag
Marked answer: D. The title tag
Why: Search engines usually show the title tag as the link, so it needs the topic up front and a clear reason to click.

Skill: SEO content writing and keyword research
Question: What is an internal link?
Options:
A. A link from one page of a site to another page of the same site
B. A link from another website to yours
C. A link that opens an email
D. A link hidden from readers
Marked answer: A. A link from one page of a site to another page of the same site
Why: Internal links help readers and search engines find related pages and show which pages matter most on the site.

Skill: SEO content writing and keyword research
Question: A keyword has high volume, but every top result is a product page. You plan a long how-to post for it. What is the risk?
Options:
A. None, volume is all that matters
B. The post may break the site
C. The post may not match what searchers want, so it struggles to rank
D. Search engines ban blog posts
Marked answer: C. The post may not match what searchers want, so it struggles to rank
Why: The results show buying intent. A guide doesn't match it, so it is unlikely to rank however well it is written.

Question: Which sentence is correct?
Options:
A. Its a busy week for the team.
B. It's a busy week for the team.
C. Its' a busy week for the team.
D. It is' a busy week for the team.
Marked answer: B. It's a busy week for the team.
Why: "It's" is short for "it is". "Its" without an apostrophe shows possession, as in "the team and its plans".

Question: In Indian number style, how is 1,50,00,000 read?
Options:
A. 15 lakh
B. 1.5 million
C. 1.5 crore
D. 150 crore
Marked answer: C. 1.5 crore
Why: One crore is 1,00,00,000 (ten million), so 1,50,00,000 is 1.5 crore.

Question: What is the main job of a style guide?
Options:
A. To list the writer's sources
B. To set the deadline
C. To check for plagiarism
D. To keep spelling, tone and formatting consistent across writers
Marked answer: D. To keep spelling, tone and formatting consistent across writers
Why: A style guide records the choices a publication makes, so every writer and editor follows the same rules.

Question: Which edit fixes the dangling modifier in 'Walking into the office, the printer was broken'?
Options:
A. Walking into the office, I found the printer broken.
B. Walking into the office the printer was broken.
C. The printer, walking into the office, was broken.
D. Walking into the office, the printer was broken today.
Marked answer: A. Walking into the office, I found the printer broken.
Why: The opening phrase has to describe the subject that follows. A printer doesn't walk, so the sentence needs a person as its subject.

Question: What does 'reach' measure on a social post?
Options:
A. How many unique people saw it
B. How many times it was shared
C. How many clicks it got
D. How many followers the account has
Marked answer: A. How many unique people saw it
Why: Reach counts unique people who saw the post. Impressions count every time it was shown, including repeat views.

Question: Under ASCI's influencer guidelines, what must an influencer do in a paid post?
Options:
A. Nothing, if the product is good
B. Mention the price
C. Clearly label it as an ad or partnership
D. Post it only at night
Marked answer: C. Clearly label it as an ad or partnership
Why: The guidelines ask for a clear disclosure label, such as #ad or Paid Partnership, that the audience can easily see.

Question: A campaign's goal is website sales. Which number matters most?
Options:
A. Likes
B. Followers gained
C. Video views
D. Purchases or conversions from the campaign
Marked answer: D. Purchases or conversions from the campaign
Why: When the goal is sales, measure sales. Likes and views can rise while no one buys.

Question: What is A/B testing in social ads?
Options:
A. Posting the same ad twice a day
B. Running two versions that differ in one thing to see which does better
C. Testing ads in only one city
D. Asking the team which ad they like
Marked answer: B. Running two versions that differ in one thing to see which does better
Why: Changing one thing at a time, such as the image or headline, shows what actually caused the difference in results.

Question: A post reached 10,000 people and got 500 likes, comments, shares and saves. What is its engagement rate by reach?
Why: Engagement rate by reach is engagements divided by reach: 500 ÷ 10,000 = 0.05, or 5%.

Question: What is the difference between reach and impressions?
Options:
A. They are the same
B. Reach counts clicks; impressions count likes
C. Reach counts unique people; impressions count every time the post was shown
D. Impressions count only paid views
Marked answer: C. Reach counts unique people; impressions count every time the post was shown
Why: One person who sees a post three times adds 1 to reach and 3 to impressions.

Question: What are UTM parameters used for?
Options:
A. Speeding up page load
B. Hiding links
C. Shortening URLs
D. Tagging links so web analytics shows which campaign and source a visit came from
Marked answer: D. Tagging links so web analytics shows which campaign and source a visit came from
Why: Tags such as utm_source and utm_campaign on a link let web analytics credit each visit to the right post or campaign.

Question: Which is a 'vanity metric' when the goal is leads?
Options:
A. Follower count
B. Cost per lead
C. Lead form completions
D. Leads that became customers
Marked answer: A. Follower count
Why: Follower count can grow without bringing a single lead; the other three measure the goal directly.

Question: Which part of a positioning statement says who the product is for?
Options:
A. The tagline
B. The price
C. The target customer or segment
D. The logo
Marked answer: C. The target customer or segment
Why: A positioning statement starts with the target customer and their need; everything else is framed for them.

Question: What is a value proposition?
Options:
A. A clear statement of the benefit a customer gets and why it beats the alternatives
B. A list of all product features
C. The product's price list
D. The company's mission statement
Marked answer: A. A clear statement of the benefit a customer gets and why it beats the alternatives
Why: A value proposition says what the customer gains and why this product does it better than the other options.

Question: What are win-loss interviews mainly used for?
Options:
A. Hiring sales staff
B. Setting office budgets
C. Training new joiners
D. Learning why buyers chose or rejected the product
Marked answer: D. Learning why buyers chose or rejected the product
Why: Talking to buyers after a deal is won or lost shows which messages, features and objections actually decided it.

Question: Which message is benefit-led rather than feature-led?
Options:
A. Built on a microservices architecture
B. Close your books two days faster each month
C. Has 40 report templates
D. Supports single sign-on
Marked answer: B. Close your books two days faster each month
Why: It says what the customer gets, time saved, rather than what the product has.

Question: What is a soft launch?
Options:
A. A launch with no marketing at all
B. A limited release to a small group to learn before the full launch
C. A launch only on social media
D. Cancelling a launch
Marked answer: B. A limited release to a small group to learn before the full launch
Why: A soft launch tests the product, pricing and support with a small audience, so problems are fixed before the full launch.

Question: Which team most needs a launch FAQ and an escalation path on launch day?
Options:
A. Customer support
B. Facilities
C. Payroll
D. Legal only
Marked answer: A. Customer support
Why: Support hears from customers first, so it needs answers and a route to the product team from the first hour.

Question: What does 'ICP' usually stand for in go-to-market planning?
Options:
A. Internal cost plan
B. Indian corporate price
C. Initial channel partner
D. Ideal customer profile
Marked answer: D. Ideal customer profile
Why: The ideal customer profile describes the companies or people most likely to buy and succeed, so the launch targets them first.

Question: A launch goal says 'make the product a success'. What is wrong with it?
Options:
A. It is too long
B. It names a competitor
C. It isn't measurable or time-bound
D. Nothing
Marked answer: C. It isn't measurable or time-bound
Why: A useful goal names a number and a date, such as 200 paying customers in 90 days, so the team knows whether it worked.

Question: Why start a new DLP rule in audit or monitor mode?
Options:
A. To see matches and false positives before blocking anyone
B. Because block mode is illegal
C. To save licence cost
D. Because audit mode encrypts data
Marked answer: A. To see matches and false positives before blocking anyone
Why: Monitor mode shows what the rule would catch, so it can be tuned before it stops real work.

Question: Which check helps a DLP rule tell a real card number from a random 16-digit number?
Options:
A. The file size
B. The Luhn checksum
C. The sender's job title
D. The time of day
Marked answer: B. The Luhn checksum
Why: Card numbers pass the Luhn check digit test; most random 16-digit numbers don't, so false positives drop.

Question: What is a false positive in DLP?
Options:
A. Data that leaked without an alert
B. A blocked attacker
C. An alert on content that isn't actually sensitive
D. A user who passed training
Marked answer: C. An alert on content that isn't actually sensitive
Why: A false positive flags harmless content. Too many of them slow the business and teach people to ignore alerts.

Question: Which is the best first step before writing DLP policies?
Options:
A. Buying more licences
B. Blocking all USB drives
C. Turning on block mode everywhere
D. Finding where sensitive data lives and who owns it
Marked answer: D. Finding where sensitive data lives and who owns it
Why: Policies protect specific data. Without knowing where it sits and who owns it, rules are guesses.

Question: How many controls does Annex A of ISO 27001:2022 list?
Why: The 2022 revision groups 93 controls into four themes: organisational, people, physical and technological. The 2013 version had 114.

Question: What does a SOC 2 Type II report cover?
Options:
A. Only control design on one day
B. Financial statements
C. How well controls operated over a period, often 6 to 12 months
D. Only physical security
Marked answer: C. How well controls operated over a period, often 6 to 12 months
Why: Type I looks at control design at one point in time; Type II tests that the controls actually worked over a period.

Question: Which standard applies to organisations that store, process or transmit card payment data?
Options:
A. ISO 9001
B. SOC 1
C. GDPR
D. PCI DSS
Marked answer: D. PCI DSS
Why: PCI DSS is the card industry's security standard for anyone handling cardholder data.

Question: What does the Statement of Applicability in ISO 27001 list?
Options:
A. Which Annex A controls apply, whether they are in place, and why any are excluded
B. The names of all employees
C. The audit fee
D. The company's yearly revenue
Marked answer: A. Which Annex A controls apply, whether they are in place, and why any are excluded
Why: The Statement of Applicability links the risk treatment to Annex A: each control is included or excluded, with the reason.

Question: Which tool shows whether an email reached a user's mailbox?
Options:
A. Message trace in the Exchange admin centre
B. The Teams admin centre
C. OneDrive sync settings
D. Windows Event Viewer
Marked answer: A. Message trace in the Exchange admin centre
Why: Message trace follows a message through Exchange Online and shows whether it was delivered, quarantined or failed.

Question: What does a shared mailbox in Exchange Online usually need?
Options:
A. Its own paid licence, always
B. No licence below its size limit, with access given to users
C. A separate tenant
D. A Teams phone number
Marked answer: B. No licence below its size limit, with access given to users
Why: A shared mailbox needs no licence up to its size limit unless it needs an archive or a hold; users get access through permissions.

Question: Where would you require MFA only when users sign in from outside the office network?
Options:
A. Mail flow rules
B. OneDrive settings
C. Conditional Access in Microsoft Entra ID
D. Teams meeting policies
Marked answer: C. Conditional Access in Microsoft Entra ID
Why: Conditional Access policies apply conditions such as location, device and risk, and can ask for MFA only off the trusted network.

Question: A user needs a file back that they deleted from OneDrive two weeks ago. Where do you look first?
Options:
A. Exchange quarantine
B. The Teams chat
C. The laptop's recycle bin only
D. The OneDrive recycle bin
Marked answer: D. The OneDrive recycle bin
Why: OneDrive keeps deleted files in its recycle bin for a set time (93 days by default), so the user or an admin can restore them.

Question: A risk is rated likelihood 4 and impact 5 on 1–5 scales, and scored by multiplying them. What is its score?
Why: Likelihood times impact: 4 × 5 = 20 out of a possible 25, which most heat maps show as high.

Question: Buying cyber insurance is an example of which risk treatment?
Options:
A. Transfer
B. Avoid
C. Accept
D. Reduce
Marked answer: A. Transfer
Why: Insurance moves some of the financial impact to the insurer. The risk itself still exists, so controls are still needed.

Question: What is residual risk?
Options:
A. Risk before any controls
B. Risk from a third party only
C. Risk that has been insured
D. The risk left after controls are applied
Marked answer: D. The risk left after controls are applied
Why: Residual risk is what remains once controls are in place; it is what the risk owner accepts or treats further.

Question: What is risk appetite?
Options:
A. The number of risks in the register
B. The amount and type of risk an organisation is willing to accept
C. The budget of the security team
D. How often audits happen
Marked answer: B. The amount and type of risk an organisation is willing to accept
Why: Risk appetite, set by leadership, says how much risk is acceptable, so teams know when a risk must be treated.

Question: What is the main reason to tier vendors by risk?
Options:
A. To spend review effort where the risk is highest
B. To pay low-risk vendors less
C. To avoid contracts
D. To skip high-risk vendors
Marked answer: A. To spend review effort where the risk is highest
Why: Tiering puts deep reviews on vendors with sensitive data or critical access and lighter checks on the rest.

Question: Which document gives independent evidence of a vendor's controls over a period?
Options:
A. The vendor's marketing brochure
B. A SOC 2 Type II report
C. An invoice
D. A non-disclosure agreement
Marked answer: B. A SOC 2 Type II report
Why: A SOC 2 Type II report is an independent auditor's test of how the vendor's controls worked over months.

Question: What is a 'fourth party'?
Options:
A. A regulator
B. A customer's customer
C. A vendor's own vendor or subcontractor
D. An internal auditor
Marked answer: C. A vendor's own vendor or subcontractor
Why: Your vendor's suppliers can also touch your data, so contracts should require notice and controls for subcontractors.

Question: Which contract clause lets you check a vendor's controls yourself?
Options:
A. Payment terms
B. Force majeure
C. Non-compete
D. Right to audit
Marked answer: D. Right to audit
Why: A right-to-audit clause lets you, or an auditor you appoint, inspect the vendor's controls and records.

Question: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, what is the person whose personal data is processed called?
Options:
A. Data Fiduciary
B. Data Principal
C. Data Processor
D. Consent Manager
Marked answer: B. Data Principal
Why: The Act calls the individual the Data Principal; the organisation deciding why and how data is processed is the Data Fiduciary.

Question: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, who decides the purpose and means of processing personal data?
Options:
A. The Data Principal
B. The Data Protection Board
C. The Data Fiduciary
D. The cloud provider
Marked answer: C. The Data Fiduciary
Why: The Data Fiduciary decides why and how personal data is processed and carries the main duties under the Act.

Question: What does purpose limitation mean?
Options:
A. Using personal data only for the purpose it was collected for
B. Limiting the number of staff
C. Deleting all data each year
D. Encrypting every file
Marked answer: A. Using personal data only for the purpose it was collected for
Why: Data collected for one purpose shouldn't be reused for an unrelated one without a fresh lawful basis.

Question: Which is an example of data minimisation?
Options:
A. Collecting Aadhaar for a newsletter sign-up
B. Keeping all data forever
C. Sharing data with every team
D. Asking only for an email address to send a newsletter
Marked answer: D. Asking only for an email address to send a newsletter
Why: Data minimisation means collecting only what the purpose needs; a newsletter needs an email address, nothing more.

Question: Under CERT-In's 2022 directions, within how many hours of noticing must a reportable cyber incident be reported?
Why: The April 2022 directions ask organisations to report listed incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them.

Question: What is the first priority when a breach is discovered?
Options:
A. Contain it to stop more data leaving
B. Issue a press release
C. Delete all logs
D. Fire the person responsible
Marked answer: A. Contain it to stop more data leaving
Why: Containment limits the harm. Evidence is kept for the investigation, and notices follow the legal timelines.

Question: Under the DPDP Act, 2023, whom must a Data Fiduciary inform of a personal data breach?
Options:
A. Only the police
B. Nobody, if it is small
C. Only the company's board
D. The Data Protection Board and each affected Data Principal
Marked answer: D. The Data Protection Board and each affected Data Principal
Why: The Act asks the Data Fiduciary to inform both the Board and every affected Data Principal, in the form the rules prescribe.

Question: Why keep logs and evidence untouched during a breach?
Options:
A. To save storage
B. To find the cause and support any legal or regulatory follow-up
C. Because deleting them is slow
D. To share them on social media
Marked answer: B. To find the cause and support any legal or regulatory follow-up
Why: Untouched evidence shows what happened, supports regulator questions and helps stop it happening again.

Question: Which is an example of multi-factor authentication?
Options:
A. A password and a code from an authenticator app
B. A long password
C. Two passwords
D. A password and a security question
Marked answer: A. A password and a code from an authenticator app
Why: MFA combines different kinds of factor: something you know, have or are. Two things you know are still one factor.

Question: What is RBAC?
Options:
A. Giving each user rights one by one
B. Giving access through roles that match job functions
C. Removing all access every month
D. Using biometrics only
Marked answer: B. Giving access through roles that match job functions
Why: Role-based access control gives rights to roles and puts people in roles, so access follows the job and is easier to review.

Question: What should happen to a leaver's accounts?
Options:
A. Keep them for a year in case they return
B. Pass the password to their manager
C. Disable them on the last working day and remove access
D. Nothing until the next audit
Marked answer: C. Disable them on the last working day and remove access
Why: Prompt disabling stops a former employee, or anyone with their password, from getting in. Data is handed over through proper access.

Question: What does single sign-on (SSO) let a user do?
Options:
A. Skip passwords forever
B. Share their account
C. Reset other users' passwords
D. Sign in once and reach many applications
Marked answer: D. Sign in once and reach many applications
Why: SSO uses one identity provider sign-in for many apps, so there are fewer passwords and access can be removed in one place.

Question: In the NIST incident response cycle, what comes after detection and analysis?
Options:
A. Preparation
B. Containment, eradication and recovery
C. Lessons learned
D. Procurement
Marked answer: B. Containment, eradication and recovery
Why: NIST SP 800-61 runs preparation; detection and analysis; containment, eradication and recovery; then post-incident activity.

Question: What is a playbook in incident response?
Options:
A. A step-by-step guide for a type of incident
B. A list of employees
C. The SIEM licence
D. A training game
Marked answer: A. A step-by-step guide for a type of incident
Why: A playbook sets out the checks, actions and contacts for a type of incident, such as phishing or ransomware, so responders don't start from scratch.

Question: Why should responders keep a timeline during an incident?
Options:
A. It is needed for payroll
B. To decorate the report
C. To know what happened when, for the root cause and any reports
D. Because the SIEM cannot store logs
Marked answer: C. To know what happened when, for the root cause and any reports
Why: A timeline written as you go supports the root cause, regulator reports and the review afterwards.

Question: Which action best contains a compromised user account?
Options:
A. Send the user an email
B. Wait for the next audit
C. Delete all their files
D. Disable the account and revoke its sessions
Marked answer: D. Disable the account and revoke its sessions
Why: Disabling the account and revoking sessions and tokens stops the attacker using it, while keeping the evidence.

Question: What does a SIEM mainly do?
Options:
A. Collects, stores and correlates logs to raise security alerts
B. Blocks all traffic
C. Backs up laptops
D. Manages payroll
Marked answer: A. Collects, stores and correlates logs to raise security alerts
Why: A SIEM gathers logs from many systems, links related events and raises alerts for analysts to investigate.

Question: Under CERT-In's 2022 directions, how long must logs of ICT systems be kept?
Options:
A. 30 days
B. 90 days
C. Two years
D. 180 days, within India
Marked answer: D. 180 days, within India
Why: The directions ask for logs to be kept for a rolling 180 days, maintained within India.

Question: Many failed logins on many different accounts from one IP, with one or two tries each, suggest what?
Options:
A. A backup job
B. A forgotten password
C. Password spraying
D. A printer fault
Marked answer: C. Password spraying
Why: Password spraying tries a few common passwords across many accounts to stay under lockout limits.

Question: What is a false positive alert?
Options:
A. A real attack the SIEM missed
B. An alert raised on activity that is actually harmless
C. An alert closed late
D. A log with no timestamp
Marked answer: B. An alert raised on activity that is actually harmless
Why: A false positive fires on harmless activity. A real attack that raises no alert is a false negative.

Question: In ITIL, what is the main goal of incident management?
Options:
A. Find the root cause of every issue
B. Approve changes
C. Restore normal service as quickly as possible
D. Buy new hardware
Marked answer: C. Restore normal service as quickly as possible
Why: Incident management restores service fast; finding and removing root causes is the job of problem management.

Question: Which ITIL practice aims to find and remove the root cause of repeated incidents?
Options:
A. Problem management
B. Request fulfilment
C. The service desk
D. Asset management
Marked answer: A. Problem management
Why: Problem management looks for the underlying cause and a permanent fix, often through a known error and a change.

Question: Priority in most service desks is worked out from which two factors?
Options:
A. Cost and time
B. Impact and urgency
C. Department and location
D. The user's grade and age
Marked answer: B. Impact and urgency
Why: A priority matrix combines impact (how many and how badly affected) with urgency (how fast it gets worse).

Question: What is a standard change?
Options:
A. Any change made on a weekend
B. An emergency fix
C. A change that needs board approval
D. A low-risk, pre-approved change done often in the same way
Marked answer: D. A low-risk, pre-approved change done often in the same way
Why: Standard changes, such as adding a user to a group, are pre-approved and follow a set procedure, so they skip the change board.

Question: Which Windows tool shows which processes use the most CPU and memory?
Options:
A. Task Manager
B. Disk Cleanup
C. Paint
D. Control Panel's fonts
Marked answer: A. Task Manager
Why: Task Manager's Processes tab sorts by CPU, memory, disk and network use, so the heavy process is easy to spot.

Question: A Windows PC has the IP address 169.254.10.20. What does this usually mean?
Options:
A. It has a static IP
B. It is on a VPN
C. It couldn't get an address from DHCP
D. It is the DNS server
Marked answer: C. It couldn't get an address from DHCP
Why: Windows gives itself a 169.254.x.x (APIPA) address when no DHCP server answers, so check the cable, Wi-Fi or DHCP server.

Question: Which command shows the IP address settings of a Windows PC?
Options:
A. ping
B. ipconfig
C. tracert
D. chkdsk
Marked answer: B. ipconfig
Why: ipconfig shows the IP address, subnet mask and gateway; ipconfig /all adds DNS servers and the MAC address.

Question: What is the first step when a user reports a problem?
Options:
A. Reinstall Windows
B. Replace the laptop
C. Escalate to L3
D. Ask questions to understand the problem and what changed
Marked answer: D. Ask questions to understand the problem and what changed
Why: Knowing the exact symptom, when it started and what changed points to the cause and avoids needless fixes.

Question: Which protocol turns a website name into an IP address?
Options:
A. DHCP
B. DNS
C. FTP
D. SNMP
Marked answer: B. DNS
Why: DNS resolves names to IP addresses. DHCP hands out addresses, FTP moves files and SNMP monitors devices.

Question: How many usable host addresses does a /24 IPv4 subnet have?
Why: A /24 has 256 addresses; the network and broadcast addresses can't be given to hosts, which leaves 254.

Question: Which port does HTTPS use by default?
Why: HTTPS uses TCP 443. Port 80 is plain HTTP, 25 is SMTP and 21 is FTP.

Question: Which device forwards traffic between different networks?
Options:
A. A switch
B. A hub
C. A patch panel
D. A router
Marked answer: D. A router
Why: A router moves packets between networks by IP address; a switch connects devices within one network.

Question: What does MDM stand for?
Options:
A. Mobile device management
B. Main data model
C. Managed DNS mapping
D. Multi-domain mail
Marked answer: A. Mobile device management
Why: Mobile device management enrols devices and pushes settings, apps and security policies to them, and can lock or wipe them.

Question: What is the usual purpose of a pilot ring for updates?
Options:
A. To skip updates
B. To test updates on a small group before everyone
C. To update servers only
D. To block users
Marked answer: B. To test updates on a small group before everyone
Why: A pilot ring catches problems on a few devices first, so a bad update doesn't reach the whole company.

Question: Which Windows feature encrypts the whole disk and is often required by compliance policies?
Options:
A. Defender SmartScreen
B. Windows Hello
C. Storage Sense
D. BitLocker
Marked answer: D. BitLocker
Why: BitLocker encrypts the drive, so data on a lost or stolen laptop can't be read without the key.

Question: What does a selective wipe remove from a personal phone?
Options:
A. Everything on the phone
B. Only the photos
C. Company apps and data only
D. The SIM card
Marked answer: C. Company apps and data only
Why: A selective wipe removes managed apps and company data and leaves the person's own photos and apps alone.

Question: What is the main purpose of a low-fidelity wireframe?
Options:
A. To agree layout and structure quickly before visual detail
B. To pick brand colours
C. To write code
D. To test server speed
Marked answer: A. To agree layout and structure quickly before visual detail
Why: Rough wireframes are quick to change, so the team settles structure and flow before spending time on visuals.

Question: Which is usually left out of a low-fidelity wireframe?
Options:
A. The layout of content blocks
B. Navigation
C. Final colours and images
D. The main buttons
Marked answer: C. Final colours and images
Why: Low-fi wireframes use greys and boxes, so feedback stays on structure rather than colour or imagery.

Question: What is an annotation on a wireframe?
Options:
A. A brand logo
B. A user's password
C. The final copy
D. A note explaining behaviour or a decision
Marked answer: D. A note explaining behaviour or a decision
Why: Annotations tell developers and reviewers what happens on tap, what the rules are and why a choice was made.

Question: What does a user flow show?
Options:
A. The colour palette
B. The steps a user takes across screens to reach a goal
C. The code structure
D. The server layout
Marked answer: B. The steps a user takes across screens to reach a goal
Why: A user flow maps each step and decision from start to goal, so missing screens and dead ends show up early.

Question: In a usability test, what does 'think aloud' mean?
Options:
A. The moderator explains the design
B. Participants say what they are thinking as they use the product
C. The team discusses results aloud
D. Participants read the terms aloud
Marked answer: B. Participants say what they are thinking as they use the product
Why: Hearing what people expect and notice as they go shows why they get stuck, not only where.

Question: What does a task success rate measure?
Options:
A. How fast pages load
B. How many users liked the colours
C. The share of participants who complete a task
D. How many tasks were written
Marked answer: C. The share of participants who complete a task
Why: Task success is the share of people who finish a task correctly, a simple measure to compare designs.

Question: Which is a leading question?
Options:
A. What did you expect to happen?
B. How would you find a coupon?
C. What are you looking for here?
D. Don't you think this button is easy to find?
Marked answer: D. Don't you think this button is easy to find?
Why: It suggests the answer the moderator wants. Neutral questions let participants say what they really think.

Question: What is the main advantage of moderated testing?
Options:
A. The facilitator can probe and ask follow-up questions live
B. It needs no participants
C. It is always cheaper
D. It needs no planning
Marked answer: A. The facilitator can probe and ask follow-up questions live
Why: A facilitator can ask why someone hesitated and explore surprises, which a recorded session can't.

Question: Which button state helps keyboard users see where they are?
Options:
A. Hover
B. Focus
C. Disabled
D. Visited
Marked answer: B. Focus
Why: A visible focus state shows which element the keyboard is on; hover only helps mouse users.

Question: What minimum contrast ratio does WCAG 2.1 AA ask for normal body text?
Why: AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text; 7:1 is the stricter AAA level.

Question: What does Fitts's law say about targets?
Options:
A. Larger and closer targets are faster to hit
B. More colours mean faster clicks
C. Users read pages left to right
D. Menus should have seven items
Marked answer: A. Larger and closer targets are faster to hit
Why: The time to reach a target grows with distance and falls with size, so key actions should be big and near.

Question: Where should an error message for a single form field usually appear?
Options:
A. In a pop-up after the page reloads
B. At the bottom of the page only
C. Next to the field, saying how to fix it
D. In the browser console
Marked answer: C. Next to the field, saying how to fix it
Why: An error beside the field, in plain words, shows what is wrong and how to fix it without hunting.

Skill: VoIP, SIP trunking and session border controllers
Question: Which SIP response means the call was answered?
Options:
A. 180 Ringing
B. 200 OK
C. 404 Not Found
D. 486 Busy Here
Marked answer: B. 200 OK
Why: 200 OK to an INVITE means the called party answered; the caller then sends ACK and media starts.

Skill: VoIP, SIP trunking and session border controllers
Question: Which protocol usually carries the voice itself in a SIP call?
Options:
A. RTP
B. SMTP
C. LDAP
D. SNMP
Marked answer: A. RTP
Why: SIP sets up and ends the call; the audio travels as RTP packets on the ports agreed in the SDP.

Skill: VoIP, SIP trunking and session border controllers
Question: Which problem does an SBC commonly solve?
Options:
A. Disk encryption
B. Email spam
C. Printer drivers
D. Getting SIP and media through NAT and firewalls
Marked answer: D. Getting SIP and media through NAT and firewalls
Why: An SBC anchors signalling and media at the edge, fixing NAT addresses and protecting the voice network.

Skill: VoIP, SIP trunking and session border controllers
Question: Roughly how much one-way delay is generally acceptable for good voice quality?
Options:
A. Up to about 1 second
B. Up to about 5 seconds
C. Up to about 150 milliseconds
D. Any delay is fine
Marked answer: C. Up to about 150 milliseconds
Why: ITU-T G.114 suggests keeping one-way delay under about 150 ms; beyond that, people start talking over each other.

Question: Which transaction shows the stock and requirements list for a material?
Options:
A. MD04
B. VA01
C. FB60
D. ME21N
Marked answer: A. MD04
Why: MD04 shows current stock, requirements and receipts for a material at a plant, as MRP sees them.

Question: What does a routing define in SAP PP?
Options:
A. The material's price
B. The operations and work centers used to make a product
C. The customer's address
D. The sales tax rate
Marked answer: B. The operations and work centers used to make a product
Why: A routing lists the operations in order, the work center for each and their standard times.

Question: What does MRP usually create for a material produced in-house?
Options:
A. Purchase orders
B. Sales orders
C. Invoices
D. Planned orders
Marked answer: D. Planned orders
Why: For in-house production MRP creates planned orders, which are converted to production orders; for bought items it creates purchase requisitions.

Question: What is a bill of materials?
Options:
A. A vendor invoice
B. A list of sales orders
C. The list of components and quantities needed to make a product
D. A routing step
Marked answer: C. The list of components and quantities needed to make a product
Why: The BOM lists every component and its quantity, so MRP knows what to plan and the order knows what to issue.

Question: Which transaction creates a purchase order?
Options:
A. ME21N
B. MIGO
C. MIRO
D. MM01
Marked answer: A. ME21N
Why: ME21N creates a purchase order. MIGO posts goods movements, MIRO enters vendor invoices and MM01 creates a material.

Question: Which transaction is used to post a goods receipt against a purchase order?
Options:
A. ME51N
B. MIRO
C. MIGO
D. MD04
Marked answer: C. MIGO
Why: MIGO posts the goods receipt (movement type 101) against the purchase order and updates stock and valuation.

Question: Which transaction configures automatic account determination for inventory postings?
Options:
A. OB52
B. SE38
C. MM60
D. OBYC
Marked answer: D. OBYC
Why: OBYC maps transaction keys and valuation classes to G/L accounts, so each goods movement posts to the right account.

Question: What does movement type 101 usually post?
Options:
A. A goods issue to a cost center
B. A goods receipt for a purchase order
C. A transfer between plants
D. A physical inventory difference
Marked answer: B. A goods receipt for a purchase order
Why: 101 is the goods receipt for a purchase order or production order; 201 is a goods issue to a cost center.

Question: Who usually performs user acceptance testing?
Options:
A. Developers only
B. Business users or their representatives
C. The database team
D. External auditors
Marked answer: B. Business users or their representatives
Why: UAT is done by the people who will use the system, to confirm it supports their work before go-live.

Question: What are UAT exit criteria?
Options:
A. Agreed conditions, such as no open critical defects, that must be met to finish UAT
B. The list of testers
C. The project budget
D. The go-live party date
Marked answer: A. Agreed conditions, such as no open critical defects, that must be met to finish UAT
Why: Exit criteria agreed up front make sign-off a check against facts rather than a debate.

Question: A tester finds a report lacks a field the requirements never mentioned. What is this most likely?
Options:
A. A critical defect
B. A system crash
C. A change request or enhancement, not a defect
D. A data breach
Marked answer: C. A change request or enhancement, not a defect
Why: A defect is a failure to meet agreed requirements. A new need is logged as a change and assessed separately.

Question: What does UAT mainly confirm?
Options:
A. Code style
B. Server capacity
C. Unit test coverage
D. That the system supports the business process as agreed
Marked answer: D. That the system supports the business process as agreed
Why: UAT asks whether the business can do its work with the system, not how the code is written.

Question: Which OWASP Top 10 risk comes from putting user input straight into a SQL query?
Options:
A. Injection
B. Cryptographic failures
C. Security misconfiguration
D. Vulnerable and outdated components
Marked answer: A. Injection
Why: Input mixed into a query can change its meaning. That is injection, and parameterised queries prevent it.

Question: What is the best fix for SQL injection?
Options:
A. Hiding error messages
B. Parameterised queries
C. Longer passwords
D. A bigger server
Marked answer: B. Parameterised queries
Why: Parameterised queries send data separately from the SQL, so input is never run as code. Hiding errors only hides the symptom.

Question: What does a Content Security Policy header help prevent?
Options:
A. SQL injection
B. Slow page loads
C. Cross-site scripting, by limiting where scripts can load from
D. Weak passwords
Marked answer: C. Cross-site scripting, by limiting where scripts can load from
Why: A CSP tells the browser which sources may run scripts, so injected scripts are blocked even if output encoding is missed.

Question: A user changes /orders/1043 to /orders/1044 in the URL and sees someone else's order. What kind of flaw is this?
Options:
A. Cross-site scripting
B. Clickjacking
C. Weak encryption
D. Broken access control (IDOR)
Marked answer: D. Broken access control (IDOR)
Why: The server doesn't check that the order belongs to the signed-in user. Every request must check ownership on the server.

Question: Which GST return is the monthly summary return through which tax is paid?
Options:
A. GSTR-1
B. GSTR-2B
C. GSTR-3B
D. GSTR-9
Marked answer: C. GSTR-3B
Why: GSTR-3B is the summary return in which output tax, input tax credit and the cash payment are reported. GSTR-1 lists outward supplies and GSTR-9 is the annual return.

Question: A company in Maharashtra sells goods to a customer in Karnataka. Which tax applies?
Options:
A. CGST and SGST
B. IGST
C. Only SGST of Karnataka
D. No GST, as it is an export
Marked answer: B. IGST
Why: A supply between two states is an inter-state supply, so IGST is charged. CGST and SGST apply to supplies within one state.

Question: Under which section is TDS deducted on payments to a contractor for carrying out work?
Why: Section 194C covers payments to contractors and sub-contractors for work. 194J is professional or technical fees, 194I rent and 194A interest.

Question: By when must TDS deducted in a month (other than March) be deposited with the government?
Options:
A. The 7th of the next month
B. The 15th of the next month
C. The end of the quarter
D. The 20th of the next month
Marked answer: A. The 7th of the next month
Why: TDS deducted in any month other than March is due by the 7th of the following month; for March it is due by 30 April.

Question: Under Ind AS 2, inventory is valued at:
Options:
A. Market price
B. The lower of cost and net realisable value
C. Cost always
D. The higher of cost and net realisable value
Marked answer: B. The lower of cost and net realisable value
Why: Ind AS 2 values inventories at the lower of cost and net realisable value, so expected losses are recognised early.

Question: Rent of ₹40,000 for March is unpaid on 31 March. Which entry is passed?
Options:
A. Debit rent payable, credit rent
B. Debit prepaid rent, credit bank
C. Debit rent expense, credit rent payable
D. No entry until payment
Marked answer: C. Debit rent expense, credit rent payable
Why: Under accrual accounting the March expense is booked in March with a liability for the unpaid amount: debit rent expense, credit rent payable (outstanding expenses).

Question: Which schedule of the Companies Act, 2013 sets the format of a company's balance sheet and profit and loss statement?
Options:
A. Schedule II
B. Schedule VII
C. Schedule V
D. Schedule III
Marked answer: D. Schedule III
Why: Schedule III prescribes the format of financial statements. Schedule II covers useful lives for depreciation and Schedule VII lists CSR activities.

Question: A bad debt of ₹25,000 is written off against an existing provision for doubtful debts. What is the effect on profit this year?
Options:
A. No effect on profit
B. Profit falls by ₹25,000
C. Profit rises by ₹25,000
D. Profit falls by ₹50,000
Marked answer: A. No effect on profit
Why: The loss was charged to profit when the provision was made. Writing the debt off against it reduces both the debtor and the provision, with no new charge.

Question: In a bank reconciliation, a cheque issued to a vendor but not yet presented to the bank:
Options:
A. Is deducted from the bank balance to reach the book balance
B. Is added to the bank balance to reach the book balance
C. Is written off
D. Needs no adjustment
Marked answer: A. Is deducted from the bank balance to reach the book balance
Why: Books already show the payment but the bank does not. Starting from the bank balance, you deduct unpresented cheques to arrive at the book balance.

Question: Bank charges of ₹500 appear on the bank statement but not in the books. What is the right action?
Options:
A. Ask the bank to reverse them
B. Leave them as a reconciling item every month
C. Book them as an expense in the books
D. Add them to the next deposit
Marked answer: C. Book them as an expense in the books
Why: Bank charges are genuine expenses the books don't have yet, so they are booked; only timing differences should stay as reconciling items.

Question: Which statement lists the TDS deducted against a taxpayer's PAN by deductors?
Options:
A. Form 16
B. Form 26AS
C. GSTR-2B
D. Form 15G
Marked answer: B. Form 26AS
Why: Form 26AS (with the AIS) shows tax deducted and deposited against a PAN, so it is used to reconcile TDS receivable in the books.

Question: An invoice appears in GSTR-2B but has not been booked. What is the most likely reason to check first?
Options:
A. The GST rate changed
B. The vendor filed late
C. The bank rejected the payment
D. The goods or the invoice haven't reached accounts yet
Marked answer: D. The goods or the invoice haven't reached accounts yet
Why: If the vendor has reported it, the usual gap is on your side: goods or the bill not received or not yet passed to accounts, so check with stores and the buyer first.

Skill: Cost records and cost audit compliance
Question: Which form does a company use to file the cost audit report with the central government?
Options:
A. CRA-1
B. CRA-2
C. CRA-3
D. CRA-4
Marked answer: D. CRA-4
Why: CRA-4 is the company's filing of the cost audit report. CRA-1 is the format of cost records, CRA-2 intimates the auditor's appointment and CRA-3 is the auditor's report.

Skill: Cost records and cost audit compliance
Question: Who can be appointed as a company's cost auditor?
Options:
A. A chartered accountant in practice
B. A cost accountant in practice
C. The company's own cost accountant
D. Any member of the board
Marked answer: B. A cost accountant in practice
Why: Section 148 requires the cost auditor to be a cost accountant in practice; an employee of the company cannot audit its own cost records.

Skill: Cost records and cost audit compliance
Question: Who issues the Cost Accounting Standards followed in cost records and cost audit in India?
Options:
A. The Institute of Cost Accountants of India
B. SEBI
C. The Ministry of Finance
D. ICAI
Marked answer: A. The Institute of Cost Accountants of India
Why: The Cost Accounting Standards are issued by the Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI) and apply to cost statements under the rules.

Skill: Cost records and cost audit compliance
Question: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 empowers the government to require cost records and cost audit?
Options:
A. Section 135
B. Section 143
C. Section 148
D. Section 186
Marked answer: C. Section 148
Why: Section 148 deals with cost records and cost audit. Section 135 is CSR, 143 the statutory auditor's powers and 186 loans and investments.

Question: Standard price ₹50 a kg, actual price ₹48 a kg, actual quantity 1,000 kg. What is the material price variance?
Options:
A. ₹2,000 adverse
B. ₹2,000 favourable
C. ₹48,000 favourable
D. ₹50,000 adverse
Marked answer: B. ₹2,000 favourable
Why: (Standard price minus actual price) times actual quantity = (50 − 48) × 1,000 = ₹2,000, favourable because the material cost less than standard.

Question: Actual sales volume is above budget but revenue is below budget. Which variance most likely explains it?
Options:
A. A favourable volume variance only
B. A labour efficiency variance
C. An adverse price or mix variance
D. A fixed overhead variance
Marked answer: C. An adverse price or mix variance
Why: More units with less revenue means lower prices or a shift to cheaper products, so the price or mix variance is adverse and larger than the volume gain.

Question: Why do analysts compare actual costs with a flexed budget rather than the original budget?
Options:
A. To remove the effect of volume and see spending and efficiency
B. Because the original budget is never approved
C. To make variances look smaller
D. Because fixed costs are excluded from reports
Marked answer: A. To remove the effect of volume and see spending and efficiency
Why: Flexing the budget to actual volume separates the volume effect, so cost variances show spending and efficiency only.

Question: A labour efficiency variance is adverse. What does it mean?
Options:
A. Wage rates were higher than standard
B. Fewer units were sold
C. Overheads were under-absorbed
D. More hours were used than standard for the output
Marked answer: D. More hours were used than standard for the output
Why: The efficiency variance compares standard hours for the actual output with actual hours worked, valued at the standard rate; adverse means more hours were used.

Question: Which form does a new employee fill to declare past PF membership when joining?
Options:
A. Form 16
B. Form 11
C. Form 12BB
D. Form 19
Marked answer: B. Form 11
Why: Form 11 is the EPF declaration on joining, recording past membership and UAN. Form 19 is for PF withdrawal and Form 12BB for investment declarations.

Question: Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, how many days' wages are paid for each completed year of service?
Options:
A. 15 days
B. 26 days
C. 30 days
D. 10 days
Marked answer: A. 15 days
Why: Gratuity is 15 days' last drawn wages (basic plus DA) for each completed year of service, using 26 working days a month.

Question: What is the usual minimum continuous service for gratuity on resignation?
Options:
A. One year
B. Three years
C. Five years
D. Ten years
Marked answer: C. Five years
Why: Gratuity on resignation needs five years of continuous service; death or disablement removes the condition.

Question: Which is NOT usually part of a full and final settlement?
Options:
A. Leave encashment
B. Unpaid salary for days worked
C. Recovery of advances
D. The next year's increment
Marked answer: D. The next year's increment
Why: F&F settles what is due up to the last day: salary, leave encashment, bonus and gratuity, less recoveries. A future increment is not owed.

Question: In parametric CAD, why are fillets usually added near the end of the feature tree?
Options:
A. They cannot be edited later
B. They make the file smaller
C. Later features would otherwise reference fillet edges and break more easily
D. The software does not allow early fillets
Marked answer: C. Later features would otherwise reference fillet edges and break more easily
Why: Fillet edges change when geometry changes, so features that reference them break. Adding fillets last keeps the model robust.

Question: Which assembly check finds parts occupying the same space?
Options:
A. Interference detection
B. Mass properties
C. Draft analysis
D. Section view
Marked answer: A. Interference detection
Why: Interference detection reports volumes where parts overlap. Draft analysis checks mould draft and mass properties weigh the model.

Question: Why is a draft angle added to the walls of a casting or moulded part?
Options:
A. To reduce material cost
B. To improve the surface finish only
C. To meet a drawing standard
D. So the part can be removed from the mould or pattern
Marked answer: D. So the part can be removed from the mould or pattern
Why: Draft tapers the walls so the pattern or part comes out of the mould without damage.

Question: In sheet metal design, what does the K-factor describe?
Options:
A. The thickness of the sheet
B. Where the neutral axis lies within the thickness during bending
C. The bend angle
D. The material's tensile strength
Marked answer: B. Where the neutral axis lies within the thickness during bending
Why: The K-factor is the ratio of the neutral axis position to the thickness, used to work out bend allowance and the flat length.

Question: Which AutoCAD command removes unused layers, blocks and styles from a drawing?
Options:
A. AUDIT
B. PURGE
C. OVERKILL
D. RECOVER
Marked answer: B. PURGE
Why: PURGE deletes unused named objects. AUDIT checks for errors, OVERKILL removes duplicate lines and RECOVER repairs a damaged file.

Question: In which space should the geometry of a part normally be drawn?
Options:
A. Model space, at full size
B. Paper space, at print scale
C. Inside a viewport, scaled down
D. In a block editor only
Marked answer: A. Model space, at full size
Why: Geometry is drawn at full size in model space; paper space layouts and viewports set the print scale.

Question: In first-angle projection, where is the top view (plan) placed?
Options:
A. Above the front view
B. To the right of the front view
C. Below the front view
D. Anywhere on the sheet
Marked answer: C. Below the front view
Why: In first angle, used in India under SP 46, the plan goes below the front view; in third angle it goes above.

Question: Which object snap helps you start a line exactly at the middle of another line?
Options:
A. Endpoint
B. Perpendicular
C. Nearest
D. Midpoint
Marked answer: D. Midpoint
Why: The Midpoint snap picks the exact middle of a line or arc segment.

Question: What does the GD&T symbol of a single straight-edged parallelogram (a flat rhombus) mean?
Options:
A. Flatness
B. Parallelism
C. Profile of a surface
D. Position
Marked answer: A. Flatness
Why: The parallelogram is flatness, a form tolerance needing no datum. Parallelism is two parallel lines and position a circle with a cross.

Question: In a hole-basis system such as H7/g6, what is constant?
Options:
A. The shaft's tolerance
B. The fit type
C. The hole's lower limit equals the basic size
D. The surface finish
Marked answer: C. The hole's lower limit equals the basic size
Why: In the hole-basis system the hole's lower deviation is zero (H), so the hole's minimum equals the basic size and the shaft is varied to get the fit.

Question: A dimension reads 25 ± 0.05. Which measured size is out of tolerance?
Why: The limits are 24.95 to 25.05. 25.06 is above the upper limit; 25.05 sits on the limit and is accepted.

Question: What does MMC (maximum material condition) mean for a hole?
Options:
A. Its largest permitted size
B. Its smallest permitted size
C. Its nominal size
D. Its size after finishing
Marked answer: B. Its smallest permitted size
Why: At MMC a feature holds the most material: for a hole that is its smallest size, for a shaft its largest.

Question: A vernier caliper has a main scale division of 1 mm and 50 vernier divisions spanning 49 mm. What is its least count?
Why: Least count = 1 main division − 1 vernier division = 1 − 49/50 = 0.02 mm.

Question: A micrometer shows +0.02 mm when its faces are closed. A part reads 12.48 mm. What is the true size?
Why: A positive zero error is subtracted: 12.48 − 0.02 = 12.46 mm.

Question: What is the job of the ratchet on a micrometer?
Options:
A. To lock the spindle for storage
B. To apply the same measuring force each time
C. To move the spindle faster
D. To set the zero
Marked answer: B. To apply the same measuring force each time
Why: The ratchet slips at a set force, so every reading uses the same pressure and operators get the same result.

Question: Calibration of measuring instruments in India is usually done by labs accredited by:
Options:
A. BIS
B. ARAI
C. NABL
D. CPCB
Marked answer: C. NABL
Why: NABL accredits testing and calibration labs, giving traceability to national standards; BIS sets standards and ARAI tests vehicles.

Question: On a structural drawing, 'M25' in the notes refers to:
Options:
A. The steel grade
B. The cement brand
C. Concrete with a characteristic strength of 25 N/mm²
D. A 25 mm cover
Marked answer: C. Concrete with a characteristic strength of 25 N/mm²
Why: Under IS 456, M25 is concrete with a characteristic compressive strength of 25 N/mm² at 28 days.

Question: Which Indian standard is the main code for plain and reinforced concrete?
Options:
A. IS 456
B. IS 800
C. IS 1893
D. IS 875
Marked answer: A. IS 456
Why: IS 456 covers plain and reinforced concrete. IS 800 is structural steel, IS 1893 earthquake design and IS 875 loads.

Question: '10 # @ 150 c/c' on a slab drawing means:
Options:
A. 10 bars spaced 150 mm apart
B. Bars at 10 mm cover with 150 mm laps
C. Ten bars of 150 mm length
D. 10 mm diameter bars at 150 mm centre to centre
Marked answer: D. 10 mm diameter bars at 150 mm centre to centre
Why: It reads as 10 mm diameter bars placed at 150 mm centre-to-centre spacing.

Question: What is shown by an RL (reduced level) on a drawing?
Options:
A. The length of a member
B. The height of a point relative to a benchmark
C. The reinforcement location
D. The road level only
Marked answer: B. The height of a point relative to a benchmark
Why: A reduced level gives the height of a point above or below a reference benchmark, used to set heights on site.
