Question: A 4-pole induction motor runs on a 50 Hz supply. What is its synchronous speed?
Options:
A. 3000 rpm
B. 1500 rpm
C. 1000 rpm
D. 750 rpm
Marked answer: B. 1500 rpm
Why: Synchronous speed = 120 f / P = 120 × 50 / 4 = 1500 rpm; the rotor runs slightly slower.

Question: Which transformer test gives the core (iron) losses?
Options:
A. Short-circuit test
B. Insulation resistance test
C. Open-circuit test
D. Polarity test
Marked answer: C. Open-circuit test
Why: The open-circuit test at rated voltage on one winding draws mainly core loss; the short-circuit test gives copper loss.

Question: Why is star-delta starting used for induction motors?
Options:
A. To cut the starting current to about one third
B. To increase starting torque
C. To reverse the motor
D. To improve the power factor at full load
Marked answer: A. To cut the starting current to about one third
Why: Starting in star puts 1/√3 of line voltage on each winding, cutting starting current and torque to about one third of direct-on-line.

Question: A transformer's efficiency is highest when:
Options:
A. It runs at no load
B. It runs above rated load
C. Core loss is zero
D. Copper loss equals core loss
Marked answer: D. Copper loss equals core loss
Why: Efficiency peaks at the load where variable copper loss equals the constant core loss.

Question: In a hydraulic system, what sets the maximum system pressure?
Options:
A. The pump size
B. The relief valve
C. The cylinder bore
D. The reservoir size
Marked answer: B. The relief valve
Why: The pump delivers flow; pressure builds until the relief valve opens, so the relief setting caps system pressure.

Question: A hydraulic cylinder has a bore area of 50 cm² and the system pressure is 100 bar. What force can it give (ignoring losses)?
Options:
A. 5 kN
B. 500 N
C. 50 kN
D. 5000 kN
Marked answer: C. 50 kN

Question: What does an FRL unit do in a pneumatic line?
Options:
A. Filters, regulates pressure and lubricates the air
B. Fills, releases and locks the cylinder
C. Controls flow, reverses and limits stroke
D. Measures flow rate and leakage
Marked answer: A. Filters, regulates pressure and lubricates the air
Why: FRL stands for filter, regulator and lubricator, which prepare compressed air before it reaches valves and cylinders.

Question: Cylinder speed in a hydraulic circuit is mainly controlled by:
Options:
A. Pressure
B. Oil colour
C. The relief valve setting
D. Flow rate
Marked answer: D. Flow rate
Why: Speed depends on flow divided by area, so flow control valves set it; pressure sets the force.

Question: In an FMEA, which rating cannot normally be reduced without changing the design or function?
Options:
A. Occurrence
B. Detection
C. Severity
D. Action priority
Marked answer: C. Severity
Why: Severity is about the effect of the failure; it changes only if the design removes or changes that effect. Better controls lower occurrence or detection.

Question: What is the RPN in a traditional FMEA?
Options:
A. Severity × Occurrence × Detection
B. Severity + Occurrence + Detection
C. Severity × Occurrence
D. The highest of the three ratings
Marked answer: A. Severity × Occurrence × Detection
Why: RPN is the product of severity, occurrence and detection, each usually rated 1 to 10.

Question: A design verification test that finds a weakness before release mainly improves which rating?
Options:
A. Severity
B. Occurrence
C. Customer rating
D. Detection
Marked answer: D. Detection
Why: Detection rates how well current controls find the cause or mode before release; a stronger verification test lowers it.

Question: The AIAG-VDA FMEA handbook replaces RPN ranking with:
Options:
A. Failure rate
B. Action Priority
C. Risk matrix by cost
D. Pareto ranking
Marked answer: B. Action Priority
Why: AIAG-VDA uses Action Priority (high, medium, low) built from severity, occurrence and detection.

Question: Which measure is commonly used to compare test and simulation mode shapes?
Options:
A. RMS error
B. Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC)
C. Factor of safety
D. Damping ratio
Marked answer: B. Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC)
Why: MAC compares two mode shape vectors; a value near 1 means the shapes match.

Question: A model's natural frequencies are all higher than test. Which is a likely cause?
Options:
A. The model is too stiff, such as joints modelled as fully bonded
B. The model is too heavy
C. The test used too few sensors
D. The material density is too high in the model
Marked answer: A. The model is too stiff, such as joints modelled as fully bonded
Why: Higher frequencies mean too much stiffness or too little mass; bonded joints that really slip are a common reason.

Question: Strain gauges measure strain:
Options:
A. Over the whole part
B. Only in the direction normal to the surface
C. In every direction at once
D. At a point, along the gauge's direction
Marked answer: D. At a point, along the gauge's direction
Why: A single gauge reads surface strain at its location along its grid direction; rosettes are needed for full surface strain.

Question: Why should the test rig's supports be modelled in the simulation?
Options:
A. They reduce mesh size
B. They only matter for thermal tests
C. They change stiffness and therefore results
D. Standards require it
Marked answer: C. They change stiffness and therefore results
Why: Real fixtures are not perfectly rigid or free; their stiffness changes stresses and frequencies, so they are part of the comparison.

Question: Which MATLAB data type is best suited to time-stamped test signals that need resampling?
Options:
A. cell array
B. struct
C. timetable
D. char array
Marked answer: C. timetable
Why: A timetable keeps rows tied to time stamps and supports retime and synchronize for resampling and alignment.

Question: In Simulink, which solver type is required for most code generation targets?
Options:
A. Fixed-step
B. Variable-step
C. Stiff variable-step only
D. No solver
Marked answer: A. Fixed-step
Why: Embedded and real-time targets run at a fixed rate, so models for code generation use a fixed-step solver.

Question: Stateflow is mainly used to model:
Options:
A. Finite element meshes
B. PCB layouts
C. Frequency spectra
D. State machines and mode logic
Marked answer: D. State machines and mode logic
Why: Stateflow models states, transitions and events, as in mode managers and fault handling.

Question: In HIL testing, what runs on the real-time simulator?
Options:
A. The production ECU software
B. The plant model of the vehicle or system
C. The test report generator
D. The requirements database
Marked answer: B. The plant model of the vehicle or system
Why: In HIL the real ECU is connected to a real-time simulator running the plant model, so the ECU behaves as if in the vehicle.

Question: A team member's performance has dropped suddenly after years of good work. What is the best first step?
Options:
A. Start a formal warning
B. Have a private conversation to understand what changed
C. Move them to another team
D. Reduce their responsibilities without telling them
Marked answer: B. Have a private conversation to understand what changed
Why: A sudden drop in a good performer usually has a cause; a private, open conversation finds it before any formal step.

Question: Which goal is best written?
Options:
A. Improve customer service
B. Work harder on collections
C. Reduce average first response time from 4 hours to 2 hours by 31 March
D. Be more proactive
Marked answer: C. Reduce average first response time from 4 hours to 2 hours by 31 March

B. CMYK
C. ProPhoto RGB
D. sRGB
Marked answer: D. sRGB
Why: Browsers and most screens assume sRGB, so other profiles can look dull or shifted.

Question: What resolution is usually needed for printed photos?
Options:
A. 72 ppi
B. 96 ppi
C. 300 ppi at the printed size
D. 1200 ppi
Marked answer: C. 300 ppi at the printed size
Why: About 300 ppi at final size gives sharp print; 72 ppi is a screen convention.

Question: Which After Effects panel lets you shape the speed of an animation between keyframes?
Options:
A. Character panel
B. Graph editor
C. Effects & Presets
D. Render queue
Marked answer: B. Graph editor
Why: The graph editor shows value and speed curves to shape easing between keyframes.

Question: Pre-composing in After Effects means:
Options:
A. Grouping layers into a nested composition
B. Rendering the final video
C. Importing audio
D. Deleting unused layers
Marked answer: A. Grouping layers into a nested composition
Why: A precomp nests layers into their own composition, keeping the timeline organised and reusable.

Question: Which expression makes a property move randomly over time?
Options:
A. loopOut()
B. time*0
C. valueAtTime()
D. wiggle()
Marked answer: D. wiggle()
Why: wiggle(freq, amp) adds random motion; loopOut repeats keyframes.

Question: Title-safe margins exist to:
Options:
A. Speed up rendering
B. Make text larger
C. Keep text away from edges that some screens crop
D. Add a border
Marked answer: C. Keep text away from edges that some screens crop
Why: Some displays crop the frame edges, so key text stays inside the safe area.

Skill: Clinical trial process and ICH-GCP basics
Question: Which phase of a clinical trial is mainly about safety and dosing in a small group?
Options:
A. Phase I
B. Phase II
C. Phase III
D. Phase IV
Marked answer: A. Phase I
Why: Phase I studies safety, tolerability and dosing, often in healthy volunteers.

Skill: Clinical trial process and ICH-GCP basics
Question: In India, clinical trials are approved by:
Options:
A. The FSSAI
B. SEBI
C. The ICMR alone
D. The CDSCO (DCGI)
Marked answer: D. The CDSCO (DCGI)
Why: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, headed by the DCGI, approves trials under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019.

Skill: Clinical trial process and ICH-GCP basics
Question: ICH E6 is the guideline on:
Options:
A. Statistical analysis
B. Drug pricing
C. Good Clinical Practice
D. Manufacturing
Marked answer: C. Good Clinical Practice
Why: ICH E6 sets out Good Clinical Practice; ICH E9 covers statistical principles.

Skill: Clinical trial process and ICH-GCP basics
Question: 21 CFR Part 11 concerns:
Options:
A. Drug labelling
B. Electronic records and electronic signatures
C. Patient recruitment
D. Sample sizes
Marked answer: B. Electronic records and electronic signatures
Why: Part 11 sets FDA requirements for trustworthy electronic records and signatures, including audit trails.

Question: Which of these is PHI under HIPAA?
Options:
A. A hospital's annual revenue
B. A patient's name with their diagnosis
C. Anonymous national disease statistics
D. A doctor's published article
Marked answer: B. A patient's name with their diagnosis
Why: PHI is health information linked to an identifiable individual; aggregate or anonymous data is not.

Question: The HIPAA 'minimum necessary' standard means:
Options:
A. Use or share only the PHI needed for the task
B. Keep at least one copy of every record
C. Store data for the minimum time
D. Share PHI with anyone who asks
Marked answer: A. Use or share only the PHI needed for the task
Why: Staff access and disclose only the PHI needed for the purpose.

Question: A US hospital's offshore medical coding vendor is, under HIPAA:
Options:
A. A covered entity
B. Exempt from HIPAA
C. A health plan
D. A business associate
Marked answer: D. A business associate
Why: Vendors handling PHI on behalf of covered entities are business associates bound by a business associate agreement.

Question: You accidentally email a patient file to the wrong address. What is the right first step?
Options:
A. Delete your sent copy and say nothing
B. Wait to see if the recipient complains
C. Report it to the privacy or security officer immediately
D. Email the patient yourself
Marked answer: C. Report it to the privacy or security officer immediately
Why: Prompt internal reporting lets the organisation contain the breach and decide on notification.

Question: An auditor checks 200 codes and finds 8 wrong. What is the coding accuracy?
Unbundling in medical coding means:
Options:
A. Billing separately for procedures that should be reported under one combined code
B. Using an older code set
C. Adding a modifier
D. Coding only the primary diagnosis
Marked answer: A. Billing separately for procedures that should be reported under one combined code
Why: Unbundling splits a bundled service into separate codes; NCCI edits are designed to catch it.

Question: Which source is authoritative for ICD-10-CM coding guidance?
Options:
A. A coder's personal notes
B. A billing team email
C. The insurer's website
D. The ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines and AHA Coding Clinic
Marked answer: D. The ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines and AHA Coding Clinic
Why: The Official Guidelines and AHA Coding Clinic are the recognised references.

Question: A physician query should be raised when:
Options:
A. The coder wants a higher-paying code
B. The patient asks
C. Documentation is unclear or conflicting
D. The chart is long
Marked answer: C. Documentation is unclear or conflicting
Why: Queries clarify documentation; they must not lead the physician to a particular answer.

Question: Which form must Indian hotels submit for foreign guests?
Options:
A. Form 16
B. Form C
C. Form A1
D. Form 26AS
Marked answer: B. Form C
Why: Hotels report foreign nationals' stays through Form C to the immigration authorities (FRRO system).

Question: A hotel has 100 rooms, sells 80 at an average rate of ₹5,000. What is RevPAR?
Why: RevPAR = room revenue ÷ available rooms = (80 × 5,000) ÷ 100 = ₹4,000, or ADR × occupancy.

Question: The night audit's main purpose is to:
Options:
A. Clean the lobby
B. Plan staff rosters
C. Order supplies
D. Close the day's accounts and roll the business date
Marked answer: D. Close the day's accounts and roll the business date
Why: The night audit posts charges, balances accounts and moves the PMS to the next business date.

Question: A room shown as occupied in the PMS but found empty with no luggage is called:
Options:
A. A sleeper
B. A skipper
C. A walk-in
D. A house use room
Marked answer: A. A sleeper
Why: A sleeper is a room the PMS thinks is occupied but is actually vacant; a skipper left without paying.

Question: Under CIF, who pays the main freight and insurance to the destination port?
Options:
A. The buyer
B. The seller
C. The bank
D. The customs broker
Marked answer: B. The seller
Why: Cost, Insurance and Freight puts the main carriage and minimum insurance on the seller, though risk passes when goods are on board.

Question: Export shipping bills in India are filed electronically through:
Options:
A. ICEGATE
B. The GST portal only
C. MCA21
D. TRACES
Marked answer: A. ICEGATE
Why: Shipping bills are filed on ICEGATE, the customs portal, usually by the CHA.

Question: To export services or goods without paying IGST, an exporter files:
Options:
A. A shipping bill only
B. Form 26AS
C. An e-way bill
D. A Letter of Undertaking (LUT)
Marked answer: D. A Letter of Undertaking (LUT)
Why: With an LUT filed on the GST portal, exports go out zero-rated without paying IGST.

Question: A negotiable bill of lading serves as:
Options:
A. An insurance policy
B. A tax invoice
C. A document of title to the goods
D. A packing list
Marked answer: C. A document of title to the goods
Why: A negotiable bill of lading gives the holder the right to take delivery, which is why banks hold it under an LC.

Question: The 'source of hire' report in an ATS shows:
Options:
A. Where hired candidates came from, such as referrals or job boards
B. The salary of each hire
C. Interviewers' ratings
D. The joining date
Marked answer: A. Where hired candidates came from, such as referrals or job boards
Why: Source of hire tells you which channels produce hires, so spend can move to what works.

Question: Time to fill measures:
Options:
A. Days from offer to joining
B. Hours spent interviewing
C. Days from requisition approval to offer acceptance
D. Number of applicants
Marked answer: C. Days from requisition approval to offer acceptance
Why: Time to fill runs from the open requisition to accepted offer; time to hire often starts when the candidate applies.

Question: Knockout questions in an ATS are used to:
Options:
A. Rank interviewers
B. Send offer letters
C. Book meeting rooms
D. Screen out applicants who don't meet a must-have requirement
Marked answer: D. Screen out applicants who don't meet a must-have requirement
Why: They automatically filter applicants who fail essential criteria, such as a required licence.

Question: Why should rejection reasons be recorded in the ATS?
Options:
A. They are shown to the candidate publicly
B. They help analyse the funnel and defend fair hiring decisions
C. They reduce storage
D. They are required for payroll
Marked answer: B. They help analyse the funnel and defend fair hiring decisions
Why: Recorded reasons show where candidates drop and support fair, consistent decisions.

Question: A structured interview mainly improves:
Options:
A. Interview length
B. Fairness and comparability between candidates
C. The number of applicants
D. Offer acceptance only
Marked answer: B. Fairness and comparability between candidates
Why: Asking everyone the same job-related questions with a scoring guide reduces bias and makes answers comparable.

Question: The STAR method asks candidates to describe:
Options:
A. Situation, Task, Action, Result
B. Skills, Training, Aptitude, References
C. Strengths, Targets, Ambition, Role
D. Salary, Tenure, Availability, Relocation
Marked answer: A. Situation, Task, Action, Result
Why: STAR structures behavioural answers around a real situation, what was needed, what they did and what happened.

Question: Which screening question is appropriate?
Options:
A. Are you married?
B. Which religion do you follow?
C. Do you plan to have children soon?
D. Can you walk me through a recent project you led?
Marked answer: D. Can you walk me through a recent project you led?
Why: It is job-related; the others are personal and unrelated to the ability to do the job.

Question: Why agree must-have criteria with the hiring manager before screening?
Options:
A. To reduce the job's salary
B. To avoid using an ATS
C. So screening decisions are consistent and match the role
D. To shorten the job description
Marked answer: C. So screening decisions are consistent and match the role
Why: Agreed criteria stop drifting standards and mismatched shortlists.

Skill: Instructional design and training content development
Question: In the ADDIE model, which phase comes first?
Options:
A. Design
B. Development
C. Analysis
D. Evaluation
Marked answer: C. Analysis
Why: ADDIE starts with Analysis of the need and learners, then Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation.

Skill: Instructional design and training content development
Question: Which learning objective is best written?
Options:
A. Learners will know about Excel
B. Learners will appreciate data
C. Learners will be exposed to pivot tables
D. Learners will build a pivot table summarising sales by region
Marked answer: D. Learners will build a pivot table summarising sales by region
Why: It uses an observable action with a clear outcome that can be assessed.

Skill: Instructional design and training content development
Question: Kirkpatrick's Level 3 evaluation measures:
Options:
A. Learners' reaction to the session
B. Change in behaviour on the job
C. Test scores at the end
D. Return on investment
Marked answer: B. Change in behaviour on the job
Why: Level 3 looks at whether people apply the learning at work; Level 4 looks at business results.

Skill: Instructional design and training content development
Question: Microlearning modules are usually:
Options:
A. Short, focused pieces of a few minutes each
B. Full-day workshops
C. Books
D. Annual conferences
Marked answer: A. Short, focused pieces of a few minutes each
Why: Microlearning breaks content into short, focused units that fit into the working day.

Question: Under contract labour law, if a contractor fails to pay wages, the principal employer must:
Options:
A. Ignore it
B. Pay the wages and recover them from the contractor
C. Close the contract only
D. Ask the workers to file a case
Marked answer: B. Pay the wages and recover them from the contractor
Why: The principal employer is liable to pay unpaid wages and can recover the amount from the contractor's dues.

Question: Who must hold a licence to supply contract labour to an establishment?
Options:
A. The contractor
B. Each contract worker
C. The principal employer's HR head
D. The trade union
Marked answer: A. The contractor
Why: The contractor needs a licence; the principal employer registers the establishment.

Question: Before clearing a contractor's bill, which document best shows PF was paid for the workers?
Options:
A. The purchase order
B. The gate pass
C. The contractor's visiting card
D. The PF challan and ECR listing the workers
Marked answer: D. The PF challan and ECR listing the workers
Why: The ECR and challan show PF was deposited for named workers, which can be matched to attendance.

Question: Contract workers in a factory must be paid at least:
Options:
A. Whatever the contractor decides
B. The company's management trainee rate
C. The applicable minimum wage
D. Half the permanent workers' wage
Marked answer: C. The applicable minimum wage
Why: Minimum wage laws apply to contract workers; some settlements and rules require parity for similar work.

Question: Which of these is a BTL activity?
Options:
A. A TV commercial
B. A mall sampling activation
C. A national newspaper ad
D. A radio jingle
Marked answer: B. A mall sampling activation
Why: BTL is targeted, direct activity such as sampling and activations; mass media like TV and radio is ATL.

Question: GRP in media planning equals:
Options:
A. Reach (%) × average frequency
B. Budget ÷ reach
C. Impressions ÷ clicks
D. Frequency ÷ reach
Marked answer: A. Reach (%) × average frequency
Why: Gross rating points add up the ratings delivered: reach percentage multiplied by average frequency.

Question: POSM in retail marketing stands for:
Options:
A. Point of sale margin
B. Product order sales manager
C. Price on stock management
D. Point of sale material
Marked answer: D. Point of sale material
Why: POSM is in-store material such as danglers, standees and shelf strips.

Question: The best measure of a sampling campaign's success is usually:
Options:
A. The number of staff deployed
B. The cost of the stalls
C. Repeat purchase or sales uplift after trial
D. The size of the banners
Marked answer: C. Repeat purchase or sales uplift after trial
Why: Sampling aims at trial that turns into purchase, so repeat buying and uplift show success.

Question: Keyword cannibalisation means:
Options:
A. Two or more of your pages compete for the same query
B. A competitor copies your keywords
C. Keywords are stuffed in text
D. A keyword has no searches
Marked answer: A. Two or more of your pages compete for the same query
Why: When several pages target the same term, they split signals and none ranks well.

Question: Which free tool shows the actual queries that bring your site impressions and clicks?
Options:
A. Google Analytics only
B. Bing Maps
C. Google Search Console
D. Canva
Marked answer: C. Google Search Console
Why: Search Console reports queries, impressions, clicks and average position for your site.

Question: A search for 'best laptop under 50000' shows mostly:
Options:
A. Navigational intent
B. Informational intent only
C. Local intent
D. Commercial investigation intent
Marked answer: D. Commercial investigation intent
Why: The searcher is comparing options before buying, so comparison pages and reviews rank.

Question: Long-tail keywords are usually:
Options:
A. Single words with huge volume
B. Longer, more specific phrases with lower volume and clearer intent
C. Brand names only
D. Keywords in the footer
Marked answer: B. Longer, more specific phrases with lower volume and clearer intent
Why: Long-tail phrases are specific, less competitive and often convert better.

Question: Which practice breaks Google's spam policies?
Options:
A. Writing original research
B. Fixing broken links on your site
C. Buying links that pass ranking signals
D. Getting cited by a news article
Marked answer: C. Buying links that pass ranking signals
Why: Paid links meant to pass ranking signals are link spam and can lead to penalties.

Question: A 'nofollow' attribute on a link tells search engines:
Options:
A. Not to index the linking page
B. Not to treat the link as an endorsement (a hint)
C. To follow it twice
D. To block crawling of the whole site
Marked answer: B. Not to treat the link as an endorsement (a hint)
Why: rel=nofollow signals the link shouldn't pass ranking credit; Google treats it as a hint.

Question: Which backlink is likely most valuable for an Indian fintech blog?
Options:
A. A link from a relevant Indian finance news site
B. A link from a random directory
C. Hundreds of forum signature links
D. A link from an unrelated gambling site
Marked answer: A. A link from a relevant Indian finance news site
Why: Relevance and trust matter more than volume; a related, reputable site is worth far more.

Question: Anchor text is:
Options:
A. The page's title tag
B. The URL slug
C. The alt text of an image
D. The clickable text of a link
Marked answer: D. The clickable text of a link
Why: Anchor text is the visible clickable text; natural, varied anchors look healthiest.

Question: Secondary sales in pharma field sales means:
Options:
A. Sales from the company to the stockist
B. Sales from the stockist to chemists and retailers
C. Sales to hospitals abroad
D. Returns from chemists
Marked answer: B. Sales from the stockist to chemists and retailers
Why: Secondary sales track movement from stockist to retailer, closer to real demand.

Question: Which code governs ethical marketing practices for pharma companies in India?
Options:
A. UCPMP
B. FSSAI code
C. SEBI LODR
D. ICH E6
Marked answer: A. UCPMP
Why: The Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices sets rules on promotion, gifts and samples.

Question: A chemist has stock expiring next month. The best action is to:
Options:
A. Ignore it
B. Hide it from the chemist
C. Tell the doctor to stop prescribing
D. Arrange expiry return or liquidation as per company policy
Marked answer: D. Arrange expiry return or liquidation as per company policy
Why: Timely returns or liquidation per policy protect the relationship and avoid expired medicines on shelves.

Question: Primary sales rising sharply while secondary sales stay flat suggests:
Options:
A. Strong demand
B. Better prescriptions
C. Stock piling up at the stockist
D. Competitor exit
Marked answer: C. Stock piling up at the stockist
Why: If stock isn't moving to retailers, it accumulates with the stockist and returns or slow orders follow.

Question: Net Promoter Score is calculated as:
Options:
A. Percentage of promoters minus percentage of detractors
B. Average rating out of 10
C. Number of complaints
D. Promoters plus passives
Marked answer: A. Percentage of promoters minus percentage of detractors
Why: NPS subtracts the share of detractors (0–6) from the share of promoters (9–10).

Question: A mystery shopper is:
Options:
A. A loyalty card member
B. A shoplifter
C. A trained person who visits as a customer to assess service
D. A supplier
Marked answer: C. A trained person who visits as a customer to assess service
Why: Mystery shoppers check service standards as ordinary customers and report against a checklist.

Question: In a survey of 200 customers, 120 are promoters, 50 passives and 30 detractors. What is the NPS?
Why: Promoters 60% minus detractors 15% gives an NPS of 45.

Question: Which is the best way to plan staff for peak hours?
Options:
A. Equal staff every hour
B. Use footfall and bills-per-hour data to roster
C. Ask staff to choose
D. Close counters at peak
Marked answer: B. Use footfall and bills-per-hour data to roster
Why: Data on when customers come lets the roster match staff to demand.

Question: A GRN in a warehouse records:
Options:
A. Goods received against a purchase order
B. Goods dispatched to customers
C. Monthly rent
D. Staff attendance
Marked answer: A. Goods received against a purchase order
Why: The goods receipt note confirms what was received, updating stock and enabling vendor payment.

Question: FEFO put-away and picking means:
Options:
A. First in, first out
B. Last in, first out
C. Fastest moving first
D. First expiry, first out
Marked answer: D. First expiry, first out
Why: FEFO issues the stock that expires first, important for food and pharma.

Question: Fast-moving items are usually stored:
Options:
A. On the highest racks
B. At the back of the warehouse
C. Near the dispatch area at easy picking height
D. In the damaged goods area
Marked answer: C. Near the dispatch area at easy picking height
Why: Placing fast movers close to dispatch at easy heights cuts travel and picking time.

Question: An ASN from a supplier is:
Options:
A. A quality certificate
B. An advance shipping notice listing what is coming
C. A payment receipt
D. A tax return
Marked answer: B. An advance shipping notice listing what is coming
Why: The advance shipping notice tells the warehouse what will arrive, so receiving can be planned and checked.

Skill: Facility services vendor management (housekeeping, security, pantry)
Question: A service level agreement (SLA) with a housekeeping vendor should include:
Options:
A. Only the monthly price
B. Measurable standards such as staffing, cleanliness scores and response times
C. The vendor's office address only
D. No penalties
Marked answer: B. Measurable standards such as staffing, cleanliness scores and response times
Why: SLAs need measurable standards so performance can be checked and linked to payments.

Skill: Facility services vendor management (housekeeping, security, pantry)
Question: Which licence must a food vendor running an office cafeteria hold?
Options:
A. An FSSAI licence or registration
B. A GST LUT
C. A trade mark
D. A drug licence
Marked answer: A. An FSSAI licence or registration
Why: Food businesses need FSSAI licensing or registration under the Food Safety and Standards Act.

Skill: Facility services vendor management (housekeeping, security, pantry)
Question: Before paying a manpower vendor's monthly bill, the best check is:
Options:
A. The vendor's website
B. The number of uniforms
C. The vendor's brochure
D. Attendance records and PF/ESI challans matching the billed headcount
Marked answer: D. Attendance records and PF/ESI challans matching the billed headcount
Why: Matching attendance and statutory challans to the bill confirms people were deployed and paid legally.

Skill: Facility services vendor management (housekeeping, security, pantry)
Question: Security guards supplied by a private agency should have:
Options:
A. Only a uniform
B. A driving licence
C. Police verification and training as required under the state's private security rules
D. A university degree
Marked answer: C. Police verification and training as required under the state's private security rules
Why: The Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act and state rules require licensed agencies and verified, trained guards.

Skill: AMC and facility equipment maintenance contracts
Question: A comprehensive AMC usually covers:
Options:
A. Only preventive visits
B. Labour and most spare parts
C. Only emergency calls
D. Only consumables
Marked answer: B. Labour and most spare parts
Why: Comprehensive contracts include parts as well as labour; non-comprehensive ones bill parts separately.

Skill: AMC and facility equipment maintenance contracts
Question: Fire extinguishers in an office should be:
Options:
A. Checked and serviced at regular intervals with records kept
B. Replaced every month
C. Kept locked away
D. Checked only after a fire
Marked answer: A. Checked and serviced at regular intervals with records kept
Why: Regular inspection and servicing with tagged records keep extinguishers ready and meet fire safety norms.

Skill: AMC and facility equipment maintenance contracts
Question: Why keep an AMC register with renewal dates?
Options:
A. To claim tax refunds
B. To decide salaries
C. For the canteen menu
D. To renew contracts on time and avoid uncovered breakdowns
Marked answer: D. To renew contracts on time and avoid uncovered breakdowns
Why: A register with reminders prevents lapses that leave critical equipment without support.

Skill: AMC and facility equipment maintenance contracts
Question: Repeated breakdowns of the same equipment under AMC should lead you to:
Options:
A. Pay more without question
B. Stop using the equipment immediately in all cases
C. Ask the vendor for a root cause and fix, and review the contract
D. Remove the AMC
Marked answer: C. Ask the vendor for a root cause and fix, and review the contract
Why: Repeat faults need root cause analysis and vendor accountability, and may affect renewal or replacement decisions.
